title: Chic Boho Clothes: Soft, Relaxed and Not Everywhere
seo_title: Chic Boho Clothes, Picked Not Stocked | Oops, Mine Co.
meta_description: Chic boho clothes with something going on up close: crochet, print, a hem that moves. Bought in small runs from Korea and Thailand, prints rarely come back.

hero.intro: Relaxed shapes with something going on up close: a crochet panel, a print you only read at arm's length, a sleeve that moves when you do. This is the softest corner of the boutique — easy to wear, easy to style, picked one piece at a time.

category.name: Chic & Boho
category.description: Chic boho clothes bought in small runs from Korea and Thailand, in fabric picked to move rather than hold a shape. A listing gives you the fabric and the flat measurements where the piece has them, and a print that sells through rarely comes back in the same colorway.

sections.heading: What makes chic boho clothes different
paragraphs: Boho gets sold two ways. One is costume: fringe on everything and a hat you wear once. The other is the version we buy — an easy shape in good fabric with one detail doing all the work. A tiered cotton skirt is just a skirt until you see the pintucks running along each tier. That is what a piece has to manage here: relaxed from across the room, interesting up close, and still yours on a normal Wednesday.

Most of ours come from Korea and Thailand, where a loose cut in a light fabric is how people actually dress rather than a summer theme. You can feel that in the make: room through the shoulder, a waist that sits where you want it, hems that fall instead of hang. Wearable first, pretty second, then both at once.

sections.heading: How we choose a piece
paragraphs: A piece gets the same checks you would make with the fabric in your hands. Shake a skirt out and watch how it settles — stiff cotton bunches, good cotton keeps moving for a second after you stop. Then turn the detail over. Embroidery should be stitched through, crochet joined rather than glued, tiers gathered evenly instead of bunched at one hip. A piece that falls apart on the second look never gets listed.

Last comes the question that decides it: have you already scrolled past this exact piece somewhere else this month? If you have, we leave it. So the edit stays short, a listing tells you the fabric and the flat measurements where we have them, and prices sit where a piece is worth rather than where it is cheapest. That is the whole difference between a boutique and a warehouse with a logo on it.

sections.heading: Three chic outfit ideas that keep working
paragraphs: One rule keeps boho looking chosen instead of thrown on: a single piece carries the volume and everything else stays quiet. These chic outfit ideas are built on shapes like these, and each one shifts with the shoes you put under it.
bullets: Flowy skirt + fitted knit. A long, soft skirt with a slim rib knit tucked at the front only. Flat boots on a Tuesday, a heeled sandal at dinner. Tucking just the front is what stops all that fabric from swallowing your waist.
Maxi dress + flat sandal. One piece and you're dressed. A straw bag in summer; a long cardigan, a belt and boots when it cools. Same dress, two seasons, no thinking.
Printed blouse + wide trousers. Cream trousers, embroidery at the neckline, gold hoops. It behaves at the office and still looks like a decision you made, not a uniform you were handed.

sections.heading: Coastal chic fashion for warm days
paragraphs: Coastal chic fashion is boho with the volume down and the light up: cream, sand, soft pink, rose and warm brown, in cotton with a linen feel and hems that catch the breeze. Because the colors sit close together, nearly everything mixes with nearly everything, which is why these are the pieces that end up in the suitcase. Three of them and one pair of sandals will cover a week away.

The Thai side of our sourcing lives here too: light cotton and silk blends made for real heat, in prints that still read well beside a plain tee. Take a look at the Thai edit if that is your weather, or the vacation packing notes if there is a trip on the calendar.

sections.heading: Chic vintage style, hiding in the details
paragraphs: The part strangers ask about is almost never the shape. It is the covered buttons, the scalloped hem, the crochet panel, the pintucks, the embroidery along one cuff. That is chic vintage style doing its job: a finish that used to be standard and now costs somebody time at a machine. It is the reason a plain cream blouse does not look plain.

Details like that also age slowly. A piece bought for one summer keeps turning up three summers later, which is the quiet argument for paying a little more once. Want the loud end of the same idea? Our statement pieces page is where the sequins and metallics live, and the chic style edit is the calm end of the same shelf.

sections.heading: Fit and sizing, before you add to cart
paragraphs: Loose does not mean one size fits everyone, and boho shapes go wrong in ways a fitted dress never does. Read length first: a maxi cut for 5'2" lands as a midi at 5'7", and one cut for 5'7" puddles on the floor at 5'2". Then sleeve width, then where the tiers start, because a tier that sits on the widest part of you adds volume exactly where you did not ask for it. Where a listing carries those numbers they are flat measurements taken off the garment, and our size guide shows you how to hold them against something you already own.

Sizing from Korea and Thailand runs smaller than US sizing, and the room disappears at the shoulder and bust before anywhere else, so trust the chest number over the letter on the tag. Caught between two sizes on something structured — a woven skirt, a jacket, anything with a set shoulder — take the bigger one. On gathered or flowing pieces, stay where you are; spare room turns into extra fabric fast. Still torn, or the number you need is not on the listing? Email hello@oopsmineco.com with your usual size and the piece you are looking at before you order.

If it does arrive wrong, returns come back as store credit: email us for an RMA number, postmark it within seven days of the purchase date, tags and labels still attached. A $15 restocking fee applies to all returns and sale items are final sale, so the return policy is worth two minutes before you add to cart rather than after.

sections.heading: New pieces, small batches
paragraphs: Prints are why this edit changes so much. A run of fabric gets used up, the studio moves on, and the same floral does not come back in the same colorway — so a piece that arrived in four sizes may never be repeated. We are not going to put a countdown clock on that; buying in small batches simply works this way. But a piece you have kept thinking about since last week has already told you something.

New arrivals usually turn up on our Facebook Live before they are listed here, and the email list hears next: one note when there is something worth seeing, nothing on the days there isn't, and a head start before a drop gets picked over. The band at the bottom of this page is where you join it — or see what is already on the site.

faqs.q: What makes a piece boho rather than costume?
faqs.a: Relaxed shapes — tiered skirts, maxi dresses, blouses with room in the sleeve — cut in fabric that moves, with one detail that makes you look twice: crochet, embroidery, pintucks, a covered button. Costume is the version that only works one weekend a year, and we leave that behind. Everything in this edit should sit comfortably in an ordinary week, with jeans or with a heel.

faqs.q: Is boho only for warm weather?
faqs.a: No, it just needs one layer. A tiered skirt works with flat boots, opaque tights and a chunky knit. A maxi dress goes over a fitted long sleeve with a belt at the waist. A printed blouse sits under a cardigan and does more for it than a plain top would. The fabrics are light, which makes these good layering pieces rather than summer-only ones.

faqs.q: What colors go with boho clothes?
faqs.a: Warm neutrals do most of the work: cream, sand, soft pink, rose and brown sit close enough together that nearly anything goes with anything. Then add one color and stop — jade, lilac, butter yellow, a faded floral, the kind of color our Korean and Thai sourcing turns up. That is roughly how this edit is bought, with as wide a color range and as many sizes as each run allows, though a small batch means some colors sell through early.

faqs.q: I'm petite. Will these shapes swamp me?
faqs.a: Some will, and the measurements tell you which. Shorter frames usually do better with a defined waist, a half-tuck, or a midi rather than a full maxi — you want one clear line from waist to hem instead of being cut into three. Sleeve width matters too: a wide bell on a small frame reads as borrowed. Measure a skirt you already wear and buy to that number, not to the letter on the tag.

faqs.q: What is the difference between boho and chic style?
faqs.a: Same standard, different volume. Our chic style edit is the quiet one: clean lines, good fabric, one detail and nothing moving. Boho has movement in it — gathers, tiers, sleeves with room, print. Plenty of people shop both and wear them together, a boho skirt under a plain knit being the easiest example of that.

faqs.q: How often do new boho pieces arrive?
faqs.a: In small batches, on no fixed schedule: a run gets bought, and it lands. New arrivals are often shown on our Facebook Live first, then listed on the site, and the email list is told when a drop is coming. Batches are small, so when a color goes it usually goes for good. Join the list at the bottom of this page and you'll get one email when there is something worth seeing, and silence the rest of the time.

cta.heading: Find something yours
cta.text: New boho pieces arrive in small runs and leave quietly. Leave your email and we'll tell you when the next one lands — that is usually how an "oops, mine" moment starts.
